questions.prompt: A rule holds a share tomorrow whenever its price rose today. Prices go up one day and down the next, again and again. What happens?
options: It gains, because it always holds after a rise
It earns nothing, because it never holds
It loses, because each day after a rise is a fall
It gains exactly as much as buy and hold
questions.explanation: This is a trend rule. On the back-and-forth path it held 3 times, each time on a day that fell 3.85%, and lost 11.1%.

questions.prompt: A price has climbed far above its recent average. Which family bets that it will move back toward that average?
questions.explanation: Mean reversion bets that a price far from its recent average will return toward it. A trend strategy would bet the climb continues.

questions.prompt: You borrow at 1% a year in one currency and earn 5% a year in another. When does this carry trade lose money?
options: When the currency you hold falls by more than the interest you earn above what you pay
When the exchange rate stays the same
questions.explanation: Carry earns 4 a year only while the exchange rate holds. A 6% fall turned the 105 into 98.7, below the 101 owed.
